blockers.quote: Minus six for the rival. So maybe the number fades the further someone is from your lane.
blockers.why: Check #6 fails: the crowd test produces exactly the expected pattern—distant strangers show zero while classmates show red.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Minus six for the rival. So maybe a bigger crowd will show you who really wants you to fail.”

blockers.quote: She laughs, and she's gone. And she still hasn't seen your face say it. Not yet.
blockers.why: Check #5 fails: “Her Back” is inserted as a plant, then the story returns to the rival hypothesis without a therefore/but connection.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Her number stays hidden. Before you risk seeing it, you test the rule on everyone else.”

blockers.quote: The same number. The same arms. You hold on through the second sixty.
blockers.why: Check #11 fails: this captions the number, arms and continued embrace already shown in the wordless peak.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “The card gets two minutes. It doesn't get to choose what you do next.”

suggestions.quote: The late-night study room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.
suggestions.fix: Earn the discovery with an action: “The late-night study room. Past midnight, his lamp is the only one left on. You cross to switch it off. His notebook is open.”

suggestions.quote: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver (c08). Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing (c08).
suggestions.fix: Cut this fact; the letter, brushes and next line already reveal her other life, while an Olympics detour cools the peak.

suggestions.quote: So, would you still say it to her face? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Keep the spoken close on the dilemma: “Would you still say it to her face? Tell us below.” Leave like and subscribe to the visual end card.

keep.quote: A card has one colour for every kind of hurt.
She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
That half-second is the other life, going past.
